claims.text: A high density of well-bonded interfaces in as-deposited HEA multilayer coatings retards time-dependent plastic deformation.
Multilayer interfaces impede dislocation motion across the layers.
Multilayer interfaces promote localized strain partitioning.
Interface-mediated dislocation blocking and strain partitioning reduce creep rates relative to homogeneous coatings.
The target multilayers have alternating compositionally complex alloy layers with sharp, coherent interfaces.
CoCrFeMnNi is an example of the HEA system to which the proposed multilayer hypothesis may apply.
At fixed total film thickness, reducing individual layer thickness increases interface density.
CoCrFeMnNi exhibits creep deformation in the intermediate temperature range of 500–600 °C.
Stress-assisted dislocation climb controlled by lattice diffusion is active during CoCrFeMnNi creep at 500–600 °C.
Dynamic recrystallization is minimal under the proposed 500–600 °C creep conditions.
Multilayer interfaces act as barriers to dislocation climb.
Thinner individual layers, and thus higher interface density, will produce lower steady-state creep rates than thicker-layered coatings.
Higher-interface-density multilayers will produce lower steady-state creep rates than homogeneous HEA coatings of equivalent overall composition and thickness.
Higher-interface-density multilayers will show reduced dislocation accumulation in the bulk of their layers.
The proposed interface-controlled mechanism applies approximately within 500–600 °C and at creep-test stress levels.
Alternative deformation processes such as dynamic recrystallization may become important outside the proposed operating conditions.
The reduction in creep rate and degree of dislocation trapping may depend on interface cohesion, chemical segregation, and processing-induced defects.

Failure to observe a significant creep-rate dependence on layer thickness or enhanced interfacial dislocation blocking or strain partitioning relative to the homogeneous control would falsify interfaces as the primary resistance mechanism.
